t: Appointed minister president of Prussia in 1862 to break a deadlock over the army budget, Bismarck governed for years without a legal budget and used three short wars, against Denmark, Austria and France, to unite Germany under Prussia by 1871.

As imperial chancellor he kept the new empire at peace through a web of alliances, while at home he fought the Catholic Church, banned socialist organisations, pressed Germanisation on the Poles and other minorities and created the first welfare state to win workers from socialism.

Dismissed by Wilhelm II in 1890, he spent his last years attacking the emperor in his memoirs; historians praise his diplomacy but argue that his authoritarian system, with no check on the emperor, left Germany a dangerous inheritance.
dyk: The only known recording of Bismarck's voice was made on an Edison phonograph in 1889; in it he quoted, among other things, the first verse of 'La Marseillaise', which a biographer took as a jibe at the French nineteen years after the war.
ev: Born at Schönhausen, a noble family estate west of Berlin
Appointed Minister President and Foreign Minister of Prussia in September and gives his 'iron and blood' speech to the Budget Committee
Prussia and Austria defeat Denmark in the Second Schleswig War, and Denmark gives up the duchies of Schleswig and Holstein
Prussia defeats Austria at Königgrätz in a seven-week war, and the German Confederation gives way to the North German Confederation
Wilhelm I is proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles after the defeat of France, and Bismarck becomes the first Imperial Chancellor
Abandons the Kulturkampf and, after two attempts on the emperor's life, has the Reichstag pass the Anti-Socialist Laws
Resigns at Wilhelm II's insistence on 18 March and is succeeded by Leo von Caprivi
Dies at Friedrichsruh, where he is entombed in the Bismarck Mausoleum

f.born: 1 April 1815 at Schönhausen, a family estate west of Berlin in Prussian Saxony; son of Ferdinand von Bismarck, a Junker landowner and former officer, and Wilhelmine Mencken, daughter of a senior Berlin official
f.died: 30 July 1898, just after midnight, at Friedrichsruh near Hamburg, aged 83, after years of failing health and gangrene in his foot
f.role: Member of the Prussian United Landtag (1847) and Landtag (1849); envoy to the Federal Diet at Frankfurt (1851–1859); ambassador to Russia and to France (1862); Minister President and Foreign Minister of Prussia (1862–1890); first Chancellor of the German Empire (1871–1890); Count (1865), Prince (1871), Duke of Lauenburg (1890)
f.known: the 'iron and blood' speech of 1862; the wars against Denmark, Austria and France and the unification of Germany in 1871; the Kulturkampf against the Catholic Church; the Anti-Socialist Laws; sickness, accident and old-age insurance; the alliance system that kept the great powers at peace; the Congress of Berlin and the Berlin Conference; Germanisation policies against the Poles
